name: Golden Residency — investor in public investments
instrument: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), 'Golden Residency' service page (ICP is the federal issuing authority). ICP's legacy Golden Visa page at https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/golden-visa/ names the enabling instrument in terms: 'In accordance with the Cabinet Decision Resolution (56) of 2018 regarding the regulation of residence permits for investors, entrepreneurs and those with specialized talents'. The current statutory frame is Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners with Cabinet Decision No. 65 of 2022 (Executive Regulations) — see notes on why neither text is cited here.
articles: Target Categories → 'Investors in Public Investments or Real Estate'; Required Documents → 'Public Investments'
quote_original: Investors in Public Investments or Real Estate Residency Duration 10 years (Public Investments) 5 years (Real Estate Investments) Key Requirements A minimum capital investment of AED 2 million.
notes: FILLS THE TWO NULLS ON THE EXISTING ROW. permit_duration_months 120 and permit_renewable true are now sourced, not inferred from prose: ICP states the programme runs 'for a period of five or ten years, with automatic renewal, without the need for a sponsor', and the investor line resolves which is which — 10 years for public investments, 5 years for real estate. The quote is a table row on the ICP page; the three cells (category / Residency Duration / Key Requirements) read in document order as quoted, so it matches after whitespace collapse but appears visually as a table. CORRECTION TO THE SHIPPED ROW: its summary, '10-year renewable residence for a qualifying capital, fund, or property investment', is wrong for property — real-estate investors get 5 years, not 10. That is why this file proposes splitting out uae-golden-visa-property-investor rather than carrying one 2m/10-year row. Documentary detail on the same page: public investment is evidenced by 'A letter from an accredited investment fund confirming the existence of a deposit of no less than AED 2 million', or a commercial/industrial licence with capital of no less than AED 2 million, or 'a letter from the Federal Tax Authority confirming that the owner/partner pays taxes of no less than AED 250,000 annually'. work_rights 'full' rests on ICP's benefit line 'The freedom to live, work, study and invest' plus 'without the need for a sponsor' — the residence is self-sponsored, not employer-tied. On the two accrual fields see the note on uae-permanent-residence; both remain false. u.ae adds one fact the ICP page does not: golden holders keep 'the ability to stay outside the UAE for more than the usual period of six months needed to keep their residence visa valid' (https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/Types-of-visas/golden-visa), which supports the shipped physical_presence_days_per_year of 0. ON THE LEGAL INSTRUMENTS: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 and Cabinet Decision No. 65 of 2022 are the governing texts, but I could not retrieve either from an official host during this pass — uaelegislation.gov.ae serves its legislation list and search results from a client-side call whose endpoint (/en/legislations/list) is returned by Cloudflare as 403 to a non-browser client, and elaws.moj.gov.ae (the host the atlas already cites for the 1972 nationality law) timed out on every attempt at TCP connect. So the instrument is named from ICP's own citation of Cabinet Decision 56/2018 and from the u.ae related-link title 'UAE Cabinet approves Executive Regulations of Federal Decree-Law on Entry and Residence of Foreigners', not read at article level. Article-level verification of 29/2021 and 65/2022 is unfinished work. NOT COVERED BY ANY SHIPPED ROW: ICP publishes three further Golden categories the atlas does not carry — Entrepreneurs (5 years, project value ≥ AED 500,000 per an auditor's letter), Outstanding Students (5 years for high school, 10 for university), and Humanitarian Pioneers and Frontline Heroes (10 years).

name: Golden Residency — real-estate investor
instrument: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), 'Golden Residency' service page. Enabling instrument as for uae-golden-visa-investor.
quote_original: Real Estate Investors A letter from the Land Registration Department confirming ownership of one or more properties valued at ≥ AED 2 million (without loans). Proof of residence in the UAE (property ownership or tenancy contract).
notes: PROPOSED NEW ROW — this route_id does not exist in the corpus yet, so the id check in research:verify will flag it; the quote check is what matters here. The atlas today folds property into uae-golden-visa-investor at a 10-year duration, which the source contradicts: ICP's category table gives '5 years (Real Estate Investments)' against '10 years (Public Investments)'. Same AED 2 million floor, different clock, and the property variant additionally requires the property to be unencumbered ('without loans'). Splitting is the only way permit_duration_months can be a filterable scalar without asserting something false for half the applicants; the alternative is to leave the combined row's duration null, which is what it is today. Note ICP words the ownership test as one OR MORE properties valued at ≥ AED 2 million in aggregate — it is not a single-property test. Accrual fields false, as for all UAE residence: see uae-permanent-residence.

name: Golden Residency — exceptional talent and specialised expertise
instrument: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), 'Golden Residency' service page. Enabling instrument as for uae-golden-visa-investor.
articles: Target Categories → 'Individuals with Exceptional Talents and Specialised Expertise'; Required Documents → 'Individuals with Exceptional Talents and Rare Specialisations'
quote_original: Individuals with Exceptional Talents and Specialised Expertise Residency Duration 10 years Key Requirements Includes doctors, scientists, inventors, creative professionals in culture and the arts, executive directors, athletes, PhD holders, and specialists in priority scientific and engineering fields.
notes: FILLS THE TWO NULLS ON THE EXISTING ROW: 120 months, renewable. The talent family is not threshold-based in money except for one sub-category, so min_investment stays null (NOT RECORDED, not zero). The only published numeric gate is for executives: ICP requires 'Executive Directors: A certified copy of the university degree certificate, a minimum of 5 years' experience certificate, an employment contract, and a salary certificate showing a salary of no less than AED 50,000.' — a monthly salary floor of AED 50,000, which the atlas has nowhere to put on this row and which would justify a separate uae-golden-visa-executive row if the schema needs it. Every other sub-category is gated on a named endorser rather than a number: doctors need Ministry of Health accreditation, scientists a recommendation from the Emirates Council of Scientists or a scientific-excellence award, inventors a Ministry of Economy recommendation, creatives an accreditation letter from the Ministry of Culture and Youth or a Department of Culture and Arts, athletes a General Sports Authority or sports-council recommendation, PhD/priority-field specialists a certified degree plus employment contract. Accrual fields false — see uae-permanent-residence.

name: Green Residence — skilled employee (self-sponsored)
instrument: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), 'Green Residence' service page. Statutory frame: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners and Cabinet Decision No. 65 of 2022 (Executive Regulations), neither retrievable from an official host this pass — see notes on uae-golden-visa-investor. Occupational classification levels are those of the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation.
quote_original: Skilled Workers Key Requirements The applicant must have a valid employment contract within the UAE. A professional classification from levels 1 to 3, in accordance with the approved occupational classification of the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Hold a qualification of no less than a bachelor's degree. Meet a minimum monthly salary requirement of AED 15,000 or its equivalent in foreign currencies.
notes: MISSING FROM THE ATLAS ENTIRELY — proposed new row, so the id check will flag it. Three thresholds, all cumulative: MoHRE occupational classification level 1-3, bachelor's degree or above, and AED 15,000 gross monthly salary. The atlas schema has min_income_monthly on residence rows; this row should carry {amount: 15000, currency: 'AED'} there — the output schema for this file has no such key, hence it is recorded here in prose rather than being smuggled into min_investment (a salary floor is not an investment). THE STRUCTURAL POINT: the residence is self-sponsored even though eligibility requires an employment contract. ICP: 'It is granted for a period of five years, with the option of renewal, and enables holders to live and work in the UAE without the need for a sponsor.' So work_rights is 'full', not 'employer_sponsored' — losing the job does not cancel the residence the way it does under a standard work permit, though the applicant must hold a contract at the point of application. DEPENDANTS: ICP states the federal benefit as 'The ability to sponsor family members, including the spouse and children, in accordance with the approved requirements' — no ages given federally. The age rule is published at emirate level: the Abu Dhabi Residents Office says the Abu Dhabi Green Visa 'offers long-term residency and more benefits to visa holders and their families than the standard residence visa. Benefits include the ability to sponsor sons up to age 25 and unmarried daughters, regardless of age' (https://adro.gov.ae/Visas/Types-of-Visas/Abu-Dhabi-Green-Visa). That is an ABU DHABI statement, not a federal one, and this file does not generalise it nationally. Dubai issues the same product through GDRFA under three service names — 'Green visa issuance (investor/partner)', high-level skilled worker, and self-employment (https://www.gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/5a925eb2-bf0f-11ed-5210-4cd98f768936) — but publishes no dependant age rule on that page. ICP also promises 'Greater flexibility upon the expiry of the residence through the provision of specified grace periods' without stating the length, so the grace period is NOT RECORDED. ARABIC PARITY: https://icp.gov.ae/services/uae-green-residency/ serves the same requirements in Arabic and carries the same figure — 'استيفاء حد أدنى للراتب الشهري وهو 15,000 درهم أو ما يعادله من العملات الأجنبية.' Both language versions are server-rendered; neither is an SPA shell. Accrual fields false — see uae-permanent-residence.

name: Green Residence — freelancer / self-employed
instrument: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), 'Green Residence' service page, Arabic version as served. Freelance and self-employment permits are issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Statutory frame as for uae-green-visa-skilled-employee.
articles: الفئات المستهدفة → 'أصحاب العمل الحر والعاملون لحسابهم الخاص' → 'المتطلبات الرئيسية'
quote_original: يجب ألا يقل الدخل السنوي من العمل الحر في العامين السابقين عن 360,000 درهم إماراتي أو ما يعادله من العملات الأجنبية.
quote_translation: The annual income from freelance work during the previous two years must not be less than AED 360,000 or its equivalent in foreign currencies.
notes: MISSING FROM THE ATLAS ENTIRELY — proposed new row, id check will flag it. Cited in Arabic deliberately: the English page carries the identical sentence ('The annual income from freelance work during the previous two years must not be less than AED 360,000 or its equivalent in foreign currencies.', https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/uae-green-residency/), and quoting the Arabic proves the two versions agree on the figure rather than assuming it. Full requirement set: a freelance work permit or self-employment permit from MoHRE; a bachelor's degree, specialised diploma or equivalent; proof of stable annual income or financial solvency for the whole period of residence; and the AED 360,000 two-year look-back. AED 360,000 a year is AED 30,000 a month, i.e. double the skilled-employee salary floor — the price of having no employer. This is the row that carries the decoupling the Green visa exists for: no UAE employer and no UAE sponsor at any point. Duration and renewability are the Green programme's, 5 years renewable. Accrual fields false — see uae-permanent-residence.

name: Green Residence — investor or business partner
instrument: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), 'Green Residence' service page. Statutory frame as for uae-green-visa-skilled-employee.
articles: Target Categories → 'Investors and Business Partners' → 'Key Requirements'
quote_original: Investors and Business Partners Key Requirements Provide proof of investment or contribution to a business venture within the UAE. Obtain the necessary licences and approvals from the relevant authorities.
notes: MISSING FROM THE ATLAS ENTIRELY — proposed new row, id check will flag it. min_investment is null because ICP publishes NO figure for this category, in either language: the test is documentary (proof of investment or contribution, plus the licences and approvals the activity requires), not a threshold. null here means NOT RECORDED, and specifically not 'no minimum' — the operative floor is whatever the licensing authority in the chosen emirate or free zone requires for the licence, which is set outside this instrument and varies by activity and jurisdiction. Anyone publishing a headline AED figure for the Green investor route is quoting a licence minimum from one emirate, not a federal residence threshold. Dubai issues this sub-route under the service name 'Green visa issuance (investor/partner)' (GDRFA Dubai, https://www.gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/5a925eb2-bf0f-11ed-5210-4cd98f768936). Contrast the Golden investor route, which does state AED 2 million — the two should not be conflated. Accrual fields false — see uae-permanent-residence.

name: Blue Residence — environmental protection and sustainability
instrument: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), 'Blue Residence' service page. ICP dates the launch to 2024. Statutory frame: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners and Cabinet Decision No. 65 of 2022 (Executive Regulations) — see the instrument note on uae-golden-visa-investor for why neither text is cited at article level.
articles: 'What is Blue Residence?'; 'Key Benefits'; 'Target Categories'; 'Categories and Submission Steps'
quote_original: Residence duration: 10 years, renewable, without the need for a sponsor within the UAE. Residence permits for family members (spouse, children regardless of age, and parents) for a period of 10 years, renewable.
notes: MISSING FROM THE ATLAS ENTIRELY — proposed new row, id check will flag it. 10 years renewable, self-sponsored. WHO QUALIFIES, five categories, each with its own gate: (1) Environmental and Sustainability Influencers — membership and participation in environmental initiatives, recommendation letters, awards from accredited entities, and 'Provide proof of financial support (of no less than AED 1 million)' with reports confirming how it was used; (2) Scientists and Researchers — 'Obtain a nomination from the UAE Council of Scientists', a master's or PhD in environmental or energy fields from an internationally ranked university, and recognised indicators such as FWCI or h-index with Scopus evidence; (3) Investors and Entrepreneurs — investment in high-value environmental projects with fully-owned capital of no less than AED 2 million, the project registered as an SME, annual revenues of no less than AED 1 million, and approval from the relevant authorities; (4) Inventors and Innovators — a patent in the environmental field plus evidence of added value and an authority recommendation; (5) Elite Specialists in Environmental Organisations — nomination by the relevant authorities, a leadership or specialised post, at least a bachelor's degree, and employer nomination letters. min_investment is null on this row because AED 2 million binds only category (3) and AED 1 million only category (4 of the influencer evidence list); pinning either to the route as a whole would misstate four of the five gates. If the atlas wants the investor limb filterable it needs its own row. HOW NOMINATION WORKS — and this is the part the marketing sites get wrong: it is NOT nomination-only. ICP publishes two parallel intakes, '1. Self-application' (apply electronically, complete the form, attach documents, pay fees, review, approval) and '2. Nomination By The Relevant Authorities' (the application is submitted through the authority). u.ae says the same: sustainability advocates may 'apply to Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security, or through nomination by competent authorities in the UAE' (https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/Types-of-visas/the-blue-visa). Two further terms worth carrying: a Golden Residence may be converted to Blue on meeting the requirements, and dependants may remain in the UAE for the balance of the residence if the principal dies. Retention is conditional and continuing — 'Ability to provide financial support. Valid health insurance. Continued fulfilment of the requirements.' work_rights is null, NOT RECORDED: ICP's Blue benefit list says residence, family permits, domestic-worker sponsorship and a six-month multiple-entry visa, but does not use the word 'work' the way the Green ('live and work') and Golden ('live, work, study and invest') pages do. The cross-link card on ICP's own Green and Golden pages describes Blue only as long-term residence. Do not infer work rights from the other two products. Accrual fields false — see uae-permanent-residence.

name: Permanent residence status (as a distinct status)
notes: THIS ROW EXISTS TO CARRY AN ABSENCE, not to assert one. It is the justification for counts_toward_permanent_residence: false and counts_toward_naturalization: false on every other row in this file, and it re-verifies rather than inherits the atlas's existing stance. WHAT IS AMBIGUOUS, precisely. (a) PERMANENT RESIDENCE. The u.ae types-of-visas index lists ten visa products — Golden, Visit, Work, Residence, Student, Investor, Tourist, Transit, Medical, Blue — and none is a permanent or indefinite status; every long-term product ICP publishes is a fixed term that must be renewed (Green 5 years 'with the option of renewal', Golden 'five or ten years, with automatic renewal', Blue '10 years, renewable'). No official page I reached describes an unlimited-duration residence, a settlement status, or a residence clock that converts into one. That is strong evidence, but it is evidence of silence: I found no instrument that says in terms 'there is no permanent residence', which is why this row is cannot_determine rather than a confirmed negative. (b) NATURALISATION. u.ae states the route in terms that leave no room for a residence clock: 'You can acquire the UAE's citizenship only through the Rulers' and Crown Princes' Courts, Offices of the Executive Councils and the Cabinet based on the nominations of federal entities.' (https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/passports-and-traveling/emirati-nationality, read 2026-08-17). The 2021 exceptional categories — investors, doctors, specialists, inventors, scientists, intellectuals, creatives and their families — are gated on the nominee's profile (an investor 'must own a property in the UAE'; a doctor needs 10 years' practice and acknowledged contributions), never on time held on any visa. Not one of the ICP Golden, Green or Blue pages mentions citizenship, and the u.ae nationality page mentions neither Golden nor Green nor Blue. So nothing in the long-term residence family creates an accrual. THE CAVEAT I CANNOT CLOSE: Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 on Nationality and Passports contains ordinary naturalisation limbs keyed to years of lawful residence, and the atlas cites that law at elaws.moj.gov.ae. That host timed out at TCP connect on every attempt in this pass, and uaelegislation.gov.ae returns its search and list endpoints only to a browser (403 to a plain client), so I could not re-read the residence-duration article to check whether time on a Golden, Green or Blue permit is capable of counting toward it. On the published administrative route the answer is unambiguously no accrual, and false is the right value for the shipped rows; what is unverified is the dormant statutory limb, not the live programmes. Anyone closing this should read Law 17/1972 art. 8 directly and record whether 'lawful residence' there is defined by permit type. status 'inactive' is a schema artefact — the enum offers only active/inactive and there is no route here to call active; it should not be read as 'this route was closed'.

name: Monitor source proposal — UAE residence products
notes: NOT A ROUTE — a proposal for monitor/sources/manifest.json. WHY GREEN AND BLUE WERE NEVER SEEN. The existing source 'uae-golden-visa' points at one product page (https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-visas/golden-visa) with keywords 'golden visa, residence, investor, investment fund'. Every term was lifted from the route already in the corpus, so the source could only ever detect a change to the Golden visa. A product launched under a new name is invisible to it by construction: the word 'green' and the word 'blue' appear nowhere in the keyword set, and the Golden page does not link to either. Blue launched in 2024 and Green predates it; both sat unobserved. Worse, the seeded URL is now a legacy path — u.ae has restructured under /Types-of-visas/, and the sibling path .../residence-visas/green-visa returns 404 while the live Green page sits at .../Types-of-visas/Investor-visa/Green-visa. A monitor keyed to product paths will keep losing pages to reorganisation. THE FIX IS TO WATCH INDEXES AND ISSUER CATALOGUES, NOT PRODUCTS. Proposed sources: (1) id 'uae-visa-types-index', url https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/Types-of-visas — the official index; it enumerates every visa product as links, so a NEW PRODUCT APPEARS AS A NEW LINK and is detectable without knowing its name in advance. This is the single highest-value addition. (2) id 'uae-icp-services-index', url https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/ plus https://icp.gov.ae/page-sitemap.xml — ICP's own service catalogue and its WordPress page sitemap; the sitemap is how I found /en/services/uae-blue-residency/ and /en/services/uae-green-residency/ in this pass, it is cheap to diff, and a new residence product lands there before the u.ae portal catches up. (3) id 'uae-green-residence', url https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/uae-green-residency/ with pages for the u.ae mirror https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/Types-of-visas/Investor-visa/Green-visa and the Arabic https://icp.gov.ae/services/uae-green-residency/ — thresholds live here (AED 15,000 salary, AED 360,000 freelance income, MoHRE classification levels 1-3), and thresholds are the thing that moves. (4) id 'uae-blue-residence', url https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/uae-blue-residency/ with page https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/Types-of-visas/the-blue-visa. (5) repoint 'uae-golden-visa' from the legacy path to https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/uae-golden-residency/ with the u.ae page https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/Types-of-visas/golden-visa as a second page — the ICP page is the one that carries the per-category durations and AED figures the atlas needs; the u.ae page carries only a summary table. PROPOSED KEYWORD SET, product-name-agnostic where it can be: green visa, green residence, blue visa, blue residence, golden visa, golden residency, long-term residence, self-sponsorship, self-sponsored, freelance permit, self-employment permit, sponsor, renewable, five-year residence, ten-year residence, salary, AED, nomination. Add 'launched', 'new residence' and 'category' as discovery terms — ICP's own Blue page opens 'Blue Residence is a new type of long-term residence in the United Arab Emirates, launched in 2024', which a name-based keyword set can never match but a launch-vocabulary one can. TWO OPERATIONAL NOTES FOR WHOEVER WIRES THIS. First, both u.ae and icp.gov.ae are server-rendered and fetch cleanly with a plain client — no SPA shell, no JS needed, and ICP serves full Arabic at the same paths minus /en/, so an adapter can diff both languages and catch a change that lands in Arabic first. Second, two hosts the monitor should be told are unreliable: uaelegislation.gov.ae serves its legislation search and /en/legislations/list only to a browser (Cloudflare 403 otherwise), and elaws.moj.gov.ae — the host cited by the existing 'uae-nationality' source and by five shipped UAE citizenship rows — timed out at TCP connect on every attempt on 2026-08-17. If that is not transient, the atlas's authority for the 1972 nationality law is currently unreachable and 'uae-nationality' is a source that cannot verify anything.
